edits.old: This service is the one ledger owner, and the case timeline reads it through the contract;
edits.new: This service is the one ledger owner and the only writer of the table, and the case timeline reads it through the contract; rwb-integration writes intake outcomes through the same contract (GAP-1511);

edits.old: - The flag `rwb.dataengine.ledger-read` gates the operation at deployment.
edits.new:
- The flag `rwb.dataengine.ledger-read` gates the operation at deployment.
- The masking version label, the personal field IDs the masking rows cover, the access-log granularity for AC-READ, the parameter rows and defaults of the access-log page and of the field-ID batch limit, and the database login name of the service are settled with Compliance, the data steward, Internal audit and the rwb-access contract owner at wave-2 policy load, contract review and build; no rule, criterion or test changes in value or refusal (GAP-2321).

edits.old: | X2 | The case is outside the caller's scope, or does not exist | 404; nothing returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
edits.new: | X2 | The case is outside the caller's scope, or does not exist | 404; nothing returned; every refusal of the case contract for such a case is mapped to this answer | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |

edits.old: Then the system refuses the call with status 404 and MSG-P4-003
edits.new:
Then the system refuses the call with status 404 and MSG-P4-003
    Then a refusal of the case contract for that case is answered with the same 404 and MSG-P4-003; 403 with MSG-P4-002 is kept only for a role with no Case record R

edits.old: and an applied version is never edited.
edits.new: and an applied version is never edited. The `actor` query parameter is optional, so a read without it is unchanged; the parameter is published in RWB-P1-E1066-CON, and the parameter and the index are added in the next API specification and Physical Schema versions (GAP-0585).

edits.old: its operation is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0586; ASM-0828)).
edits.new: the write carries the user, role, case ID, data product, field ID and time and no value, through the rwb-access access-log contract or, until that contract is published, the platform PII logging path; its retry rule is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0586; ASM-0828)).

edits.old: - The scope answer and the masking answer are never cached: a stale scope answer is a scope leak, a stale masking answer can disclose a summary, and a call that does not answer inside 2 s either refuses the read (scope) or masks it (masking).
edits.new:
- The scope answer and the masking answer are never cached: a stale scope answer is a scope leak, a stale masking answer can disclose a summary, and a call that does not answer inside 2 s either refuses the read (scope) or masks it (masking).
- The scope, authorise and masking calls of the read run concurrently, each one hop from this service with its 2 s budget and a breaker, and no further nesting; the parameters and the channel list are read from their versioned cache (GAP-0587).

edits.old: Its states are Loading (skeleton rows), Empty (a sentence that no interaction is recorded on the case) and Error (the message of section 14 above the panel); a masked summary shows as `MASKED`. This story serves the data behind those states and renders none of them.
edits.new: Its states are Loading (skeleton rows), Empty (a sentence that no interaction is recorded on the case), Error (the message of section 14 above the panel) and No access (the 403 and MSG-P4-002 of section 4 step 7); the screen specification lacks Empty, Error and No access, so their visual form is Not specified in the source documents (CG-ALL-2329). A masked summary shows as `MASKED`. SCR-04 has the same four states, and the screen specification lacks Empty, Error and No access for it too, so their visual form is Not specified in the source documents (CG-ALL-2330). This story serves the data behind those states and renders none of them.
